title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
notes: llm_judge: must-cite - the founding LLM-as-a-judge study; names position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias and limited reasoning ability, and is the paradigm the May Tribunal inherited.

title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
authors: Arjun Panickssery, Samuel R. Bowman, Shi Feng
notes: llm_judge: must-cite - the canonical self-preference result (self-recognition linearly, and by their fine-tuning tests causally, tied to self-preference); answers the reviewers' circularity objection.

title: Judging the Judges: Evaluating Alignment and Vulnerabilities in LLMs-as-Judges
notes: llm_judge: must-cite - even the best of 13 judges stay well below inter-human agreement on a clean QA task, and high percent agreement hides large score gaps; the case for chance-corrected agreement with the experts.

title: Preference Leakage: A Contamination Problem in LLM-as-a-judge
notes: llm_judge: must-cite - judges favour models related to them (same model, inheritance, same family), a bias harder to detect than others; direct support for a judge from a family outside the roster.

title: Play Favorites: A Statistical Method to Measure Self-Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
notes: llm_judge: must-cite - with expert human annotations as the quality anchor, GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet score their own outputs higher and also their own family's; the family-bias objection, measured.

title: Great Models Think Alike and this Undermines AI Oversight
notes: llm_judge: must-cite - judge scores favour models whose mistakes resemble the judge's (CAPA), and mistakes grow more similar with capability; a frontier panel is neither unbiased nor independent.

title: Correlated Errors in Large Language Models
notes: llm_judge: must-cite - across 350+ LLMs, models agree on 60% of shared errors on one dataset, and larger, more accurate models are highly correlated even across providers; undercuts the PoLL independence assumption.

title: JudgeBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-based Judges
notes: llm_judge: must-cite - on response pairs labelled by objective correctness (knowledge, reasoning, math, coding) strong judges such as GPT-4o are only slightly better than random; the judge benchmark for technical content.

title: No Free Labels: Limitations of LLM-as-a-Judge Without Human Grounding
notes: llm_judge: must-cite - against finance experts' labels, judges without a reference agree with experts mainly on questions they can answer themselves, and expert references largely fix it; grounds giving the judge the gold milestones.

title: Self-Preference Bias in Rubric-Based Evaluation of Large Language Models
authors: José Pombal, Ricardo Rei, André F. T. Martins
notes: llm_judge: must-cite - self-preference persists in binary verdicts on objective, programmatically verifiable rubric items (IFEval, LiveCodeBench) and ensembling reduces but does not remove it; the closest analogue to milestone-level judging.

title: From Accuracy to Robustness: A Study of Rule- and Model-based Verifiers in Mathematical Reasoning
notes: llm_judge: must-cite - rule-based answer checkers miss equivalent answer formats (false negatives) while model-based verifiers are open to reward hacking (false positives); frames the deterministic answer check and its limits. First posted as 'Pitfalls of Rule- and Model-based Verifiers'.

title: G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment
notes: llm_judge: should-cite - foundational LLM evaluator; reports that BLEU and ROUGE correlate weakly with human judgement and flags a bias of LLM evaluators toward LLM-written text.

title: Self-Preference Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
authors: Koki Wataoka, Tsubasa Takahashi, Ryokan Ri
notes: llm_judge: should-cite - quantifies GPT-4's self-preference and ties it to lower perplexity (familiarity) regardless of authorship, a mechanism that extends to same-family judges.

title: Justice or Prejudice? Quantifying Biases in LLM-as-a-Judge
notes: llm_judge: should-cite - the standard taxonomy of 12 judge biases with an automated probe (CALM); one citation for position, verbosity, authority and self-enhancement bias.

title: A Survey on LLM-as-a-Judge
notes: llm_judge: should-cite - the most widely used survey; covers consistency, bias mitigation and how judge reliability should itself be evaluated.

title: Do LLM Evaluators Prefer Themselves for a Reason?
notes: llm_judge: should-cite - on verifiable math, factual and code tasks most of strong models' self-preference is legitimate, but harmful self-preference persists where the judge erred as a generator, i.e. on exactly the items that test error detection.

title: Are LLM Evaluators Really Narcissists? Sanity Checking Self-Preference Evaluations
notes: llm_judge: should-cite - against an evaluator-quality baseline only 51% of prior self-preference examples stay significant; the balanced citation, and a reason to avoid the confound by design (non-roster judge) rather than estimate it.

title: Agreement Overstates Evidence: Error Dependence in LLM Judge Consensus
authors: Elias Hossain, Niloofar Yousefi, Ser-Nam Lim
notes: llm_judge: should-cite - ten judges carry about as much information as 3.5 independent ones, and dependence is strongest among frontier judges from different providers; quantifies why a three-judge panel is not three votes.

title: Beyond Consensus: Mitigating the Agreeableness Bias in LLM Judge Evaluations
notes: llm_judge: should-cite - judges accept valid outputs (TPR 96%) but reject few invalid ones (TNR under 25%), and majority voting does not fix it; matches the low judge recall on planted defects.

title: LLMs instead of Human Judges? A Large Scale Empirical Study across 20 NLP Evaluation Tasks
notes: llm_judge: should-cite - across 20 human-annotated datasets judge reliability varies with the property judged, the annotators' expertise and the text's source; concludes judges must be validated against humans before use.

title: LLM-as-a-judge validity is strongly task-dependent across physics assessment formats
notes: llm_judge: should-cite - frontier judges against human markers in physics: rank agreement above 0.6 on structured questions, improved by official solutions and degraded by false ones, near zero on essays; the closest technical-domain meta-evaluation.

title: QEDBENCH: Quantifying the Alignment Gap in Automated Evaluation of University-Level Mathematical Proofs
notes: llm_judge: should-cite - 7 judges against 1,000+ hours of expert grading of university-level proofs; several frontier judges inflate scores; expert-anchored evidence of judge leniency in mathematics.

title: How to Correctly Report LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluations
notes: llm_judge: should-cite - corrects judge-based scores using the judge's sensitivity and specificity on a human-labelled calibration set, with confidence intervals; the expert-labelled traces can serve as that set.

title: Limitations of the LLM-as-a-Judge Approach for Evaluating LLM Outputs in Expert Knowledge Tasks
notes: llm_judge: optional - subject-matter experts agreed with LLM judges only 68% (dietetics) and 64% (mental health) of the time on domain tasks; the standard citation that expert-knowledge evaluation needs experts in the loop.

title: Evaluating Judges as Evaluators: The JETTS Benchmark of LLM-as-Judges as Test-Time Scaling Evaluators
notes: llm_judge: optional - judges on math, code and instruction following match outcome reward models at reranking but trail process reward models in step-level beam search, and their critiques do not help refinement.

title: One Token to Fool LLM-as-a-Judge
notes: llm_judge: optional - superficial 'master key' responses (symbols, generic reasoning openers) draw false-positive verdicts from generative reward models, GPT-o1 and Claude-4 included; another reason to keep answer checking deterministic.

title: Trust or Escalate: LLM Judges with Provable Guarantees for Human Agreement
authors: Jaehun Jung, Faeze Brahman, Yejin Choi
notes: llm_judge: optional - selective, cascaded judging that escalates only low-confidence items, with a guarantee of human agreement; precedent for sending only unsettled milestones to a judge.

title: Limits to scalable evaluation at the frontier: LLM as Judge won't beat twice the data
authors: Florian E. Dorner, Vivian Y. Nastl, Moritz Hardt
notes: llm_judge: optional - when the judge is no more accurate than the evaluated model, debiasing can at most halve the ground-truth labels needed; why frontier evaluation keeps expert labels.

title: JuryProbe: An Empirical Consensus-Risk Diagnostic for Routing Reference-Free Factuality Judge Panels to Grounded Verification
notes: llm_judge: optional - reference-free judge panels share false negatives, and routing their accepts to reference-grounded checks removes unanimous false consensus; supports grounding over agreement.

title: LLM Judge Validation Under Sparse Overlap: From Inference to Design
authors: Junxuan Li, Arko Mukherjee, Soumyabrata Pal
notes: llm_judge: optional - with sparse overlap between human labels, judge-validation decisions are often wrong; gives minimum-overlap and stratified-allocation rules relevant to the expert-label design.
